{"chapter_id":"4B","issues":[{"question_id":"4B.1","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0010-E022","BATCH-0028-E011","BATCH-0028-E014"],"explanation":"The answer omits material contrary evidence on election-related violence, military-school polling allegations, women’s representation, post-election protest suppression, and the broader observer characterization of the election as highly contested."},{"question_id":"4B.2","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0029-E004","BATCH-0029-E005"],"explanation":"Formal budget-governance, consultation, and audit rules are peripheral to whether the ruler manipulated institutions to entrench power, and the answer does not show implementation or connect them to electoral or coercive restraint."},{"question_id":"4B.2","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0006-E004","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0002-E014","BATCH-0010-E020"],"explanation":"The answer omits direct evidence of blocking opposition travel and sit-ins, arresting Diongo, exclusionary aligned-official rhetoric, banning the post-election opposition march, party-linked attacks, and perceived CENI proximity to government."},{"question_id":"4B.2","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E016","BATCH-0011-E019"],"explanation":"The answer presents support for Wazalendo/FDLR, private military personnel, and armed drones as entrenchment risks even though the cited evidence does not establish that these security choices were made to preserve personal or party power; they should be clearly separated as coercive-capacity evidence rather than weighted as entrenchment proof."},{"question_id":"4B.3","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E011","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0027-E004","BATCH-0027-E005","BATCH-0021-E009"],"explanation":"The answer omits several material 2023 incidents: detention of Shilo FM journalists, arrests of Bakuka, Kayiba, and Ngongo Lomango, the July MLC-linked journalist attack, suspected ruling-party attacks, and the banned December opposition protest."},{"question_id":"4B.3","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0010-E022","BATCH-0025-E008"],"explanation":"The answer does not explicitly incorporate the post-election protest suppression or the broader RSF finding that journalists faced pressure, disappearance, attacks, and impunity across the information environment."},{"question_id":"4B.3","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0025-E011","BATCH-0025-E012"],"explanation":"Although some corrective evidence is mentioned, the answer does not clearly state the qualifying fact that there was no supplied finding of a nationwide internet restriction and that several detained journalists were ultimately released or had cases unresolved rather than adjudicated."},{"question_id":"4B.4","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E016","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0020-E013","BATCH-0011-E014"],"explanation":"The answer omits evidence on unexplained Constitutional Court decisions, corruption suspicions involving electoral judges, perceived court subservience, judicial influence-peddling concerns, and the National Commission on Human Rights’ limited effectiveness and access constraints."},{"question_id":"4B.4","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0023-E015"],"explanation":"Candidate validation and a CENI-reported register audit are treated as meaningful checks, but neither source establishes institutional independence or practical constraint on Tshisekedi; their probative weight should be limited to formal capacity and procedural activity."},{"question_id":"4B.5","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0029-E004","BATCH-0023-E017","BATCH-0009-E004"],"explanation":"Budget rules, labor-inspection planning, magistrate training, and justice-access outputs provide weak evidence about politically neutral appointments, dismissals, loyalty tests, or personality cults and receive disproportionate prominence in the answer."},{"question_id":"4B.5","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E014","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0010-E020","BATCH-0028-E021","BATCH-0012-R09-E002"],"explanation":"The answer omits the July appointments across public enterprises and regulatory bodies, the March cabinet reshuffle, the Gécamines appointments, CENI leadership concerns, reported sympathetic judicial appointments, and the available evidence on presidentialist or loyalty-oriented rhetoric."},{"question_id":"4B.6","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E026","BATCH-0006-E009","BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0027-E002","BATCH-0027-E003"],"explanation":"The answer omits the RSF country ranking, OLPA’s evidence of under-resourced provincial media regulation, attacks on journalists during the campaign, Bujakera-related press repression, and the CSAC shutdown of Perfect Télévision."},{"question_id":"4B.6","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0028-E007","BATCH-0022-E006"],"explanation":"The answer does not adequately present the qualifying evidence that the supplied record found no internet restriction, that CENI used external-audit procedures, that the EU mission was initially invited, and that Tshisekedi claimed an improvement in the RSF ranking, even though the last claim is self-reported."},{"question_id":"4B.6","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E026","BATCH-0025-E028"],"explanation":"The answer should distinguish the 2023 RSF index and the broader five-year journalist-arrest total from strictly 2023 incidents; otherwise aggregate term-period evidence risks being read as target-year evidence."},{"question_id":"4B.7","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0002-E014","BATCH-0006-E004"],"explanation":"The answer does not separately incorporate opposition travel restrictions, blocked rallies, arrests, ruling-party-linked violence, sexual violence against opposition supporters, and exclusionary ethnic-regional rhetoric as evidence of unequal political access."},{"question_id":"4B.7","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E009","BATCH-0026-E010","BATCH-0022-E010"],"explanation":"Several gender, education, displacement, and school-closure indicators are baseline or contextual evidence rather than direct measures of 2023 ruler action; the answer should label their temporal and causal limits more explicitly."},{"question_id":"4B.8","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0006-E006","BATCH-0007-E001","BATCH-0015-E001","BATCH-0018-E006"],"explanation":"The answer omits the CENCO-ECC call for corrective compilation, the coalition representative’s appeal to accept results, the Court’s formal confirmation, the presidential candidacy record, and the distinction between institutional confirmation and personal acceptance of an adverse result."},{"question_id":"4B.8","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0028-E018"],"explanation":"The answer does not include the evidence that prior electoral reforms were largely unimplemented and that CENI and the Constitutional Court remained perceived as politicized, which is directly relevant to the credibility of succession safeguards."},{"question_id":"4B.8","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E008","BATCH-0018-E009"],"explanation":"The answer does not clearly state that CENI’s voting-closure communiqué and the Court’s final legal formality occurred through institutions, while the latter occurred in January 2024 and cannot silently expand the 2023 period."},{"question_id":"4B.9","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0028-E007"],"explanation":"The answer omits the supplied finding that there was no internet restriction, disruption, or online-content censorship, a material qualification for the digital-controls component."},{"question_id":"4B.9","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0028-E007"],"explanation":"CENI register-audit terms and EU observation arrangements are not surveillance oversight or evidence of lawful digital-control supervision; their inclusion as qualifying evidence risks conflating electoral transparency with surveillance governance."},{"question_id":"4B.9","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E011","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0027-E002","BATCH-0027-E003"],"explanation":"The answer omits the broader pattern of journalist detention, phone retention, party-linked attacks, and media shutdowns that bears on administrative harassment and political suppression, while still needing to distinguish these from spyware or interception evidence."},{"question_id":"4B.10","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0025-E009","BATCH-0009-E004"],"explanation":"The answer gives formal audit, a 12% decline in documented violations, and UNDP-supported justice outputs substantial favorable weight without sufficiently emphasizing that the audit was CENI-reported, the decline may reflect reporting/conflict conditions, and the justice outputs were partner-supported rather than independently durable reforms."},{"question_id":"4B.10","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0028-E014","BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0019-E006"],"explanation":"The synthesis omits campaign administrative-resource abuse and violence, party-linked election violence, formal judicial appointments and reorganizations, and the way those personnel changes complicate claims of independent institutional strengthening."},{"question_id":"4B.10","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0025-E026","BATCH-0028-E015","BATCH-0028-E018"],"explanation":"The answer does not synthesize the independent press-freedom record, including the 2023 RSF ranking, journalist repression, broader state-authority pressure, and unresolved accountability, despite political information being central to democratic resilience."},{"question_id":"4B.10","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0013-E010"],"explanation":"Later publications are usable retrospectively for 2023, but the answer should explicitly identify their publication timing and avoid presenting first-term or post-election assessments as contemporaneous 2023 outcomes."}],"overall_assessment":"The draft is generally cautious, attribution-aware, and evidence-grounded, but it remains incomplete against the supplied candidate index. The largest defects are omitted opposition and party-linked repression, incomplete media and digital-freedom coverage, underdeveloped appointment and institutional-capture evidence, and occasional over-weighting of formal rules or procedural activity that do not establish practical independence. No score is assigned."}
